notes:
Account background: Glasswing builds an internal code search + knowledge platform for engineering orgs (monorepos + binary artifacts). Primary buy is to replace an aging in-house vector store and provide enterprise SSO/SCIM and audit trails. They ingest a very large embedding corpus (approx 250M vectors today, expect growth to 1B by EOY with frequent re-indexing).

Key stakeholders: Eng infra (SRE lead: Marco Ruiz), Head of Search (Elena Park), Security/compliance (Dirk Hansen). Decision committee: infra + security + procurement.

Requirements summary (from discovery calls):
- Workload: low-latency code search + reranking pipeline. Embeddings used for retrieval (dense) + cross-encoder reranker for top-50.
- Indexing scale: current corpus ~250M vectors, need delta-only reindexes nightly plus smaller per-pr-service streams (near-real-time).
- Latency targets: P50 < 40ms, P95 < 120ms for retrieval+rerrank on dedicated capacity; 99th needs graceful fallback.
- Throughput: peak 1.2k qps sustained during CI-driven search spikes; average 150 qps.
- Cost sensitivity: cost-per-query target ~<$0.015 end-to-end; want clear cost model and operator controls (batching, cache TTLs).
- Model preferences: open models for embeddings (custom fine-tuned embedder), allow quantized variants for rerankers; fallback to smaller cross-encoder on capacity pressure.
- Routing/fallback: prefer regional routing (NA primary, EU DR), auto-fallback to smaller model variant w/ tracing for regressions.
- Security: SSO/SAML + SCIM provisioning, audit logging retention 1 year, customer-managed KMS, strong data residency controls.

POC scope (agreed):
- 2-week retrieval latency benchmark at their scale (ingest subset ~50M vectors) using Redwood Dedicated.
- Reranking latency + MRR delta using cross-encoder on GPU-backed dedicated nodes.
- Cost modeling: per-query token and GPU cost breakdown, suggestions from Redwood Optimize for batching/quantization.
- Integration: SAML test tenant + VPC peering.
